question: What is the smallest building block of the human body that can live and do work on its own?
explanation: You can think of the cell as the basic building block of your entire body. Every tiny action that keeps you alive starts right here! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to understand how cells work?

options.C: To know how diseases start and how the body heals
options.D: To guess when a patient will be discharged

explanation: Spot on! When sickness strikes or healing happens, it all starts at the microscopic cell level. Knowing this helps you be a better nurse. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h1)

question: Where do all new cells in our bodies come from?
explanation: New cells don't just pop up out of nowhere—they always come from older cells dividing to make new ones! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is a main rule of cell theory?

options.A: Cells can form from liquid waste
options.B: Dead cells turn back into active cells
options.C: Only major organs are made of living cells
options.D: The cell is the basic unit of life

explanation: Cell theory simply reminds us that cells are the fundamental building blocks of all living things—including your patients! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which part of a cell acts like a gatekeeper, deciding what goes in and out?
explanation: Think of the plasma membrane as a secure fence around the cell. It lets the good nutrients in and keeps harmful stuff out. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main job of the nucleus inside a human cell?

options.A: Holding the DNA and directing cell activities
options.B: Pumping water out to stop swelling

explanation: The nucleus is like the control center or brain of the cell. It holds the DNA blueprint that tells the cell what to do. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which cell part is famously known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
explanation: You got it! Mitochondria generate the chemical energy that powers all the cell's daily activities. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the main job of lysosomes in a cell?

options.A: Making fats for the cell membrane
options.D: Storing water to keep the cell firm

explanation: Lysosomes are the cleanup crew! They use special enzymes to digest worn-out cell parts and waste safely. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h4)

question: What type of cell division creates two identical body cells?
explanation: Mitosis is how your body grows and heals everyday tissues by making exact copies of your body cells. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is meiosis so important for human reproduction?

options.B: It repairs torn muscle after a workout
options.C: It boosts energy production in body organs
options.D: It cuts the chromosome number in half for sex cells

explanation: Meiosis is special because it creates egg and sperm cells with half the normal chromosomes, ensuring a baby gets the right total when fertilization happens. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which condition involves cells dividing rapidly and out of control?
explanation: Cancer happens when normal cell growth signals fail, causing cells to multiply wildly and form tumors. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h6)

question: What happens to a cell when it is starved of oxygen (hypoxia)?

options.A: Mitochondria fail and the cell may die
options.C: It starts making extra structural proteins

explanation: Oxygen is fuel for the powerhouse mitochondria. Without it, energy production drops fast, putting the cell's survival at risk. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h6)
